headline: VIDEOCON INDUSTRIES: Supreme Court on Nov 16, 2026 dismisses Twinstar's appeals; Rs. 2,962.02 crore plan stays set aside
facts: Supreme Court order dated November 16, 2026 dismissed Civil Appeal Nos. 894, 512 and 509 of 2022 filed by Twinstar Technologies Limited, the Successful Resolution Applicant. The NCLAT's 05.01.2022 order setting aside the plan and remitting it to the Committee of Creditors (CoC) therefore stands.

The Court held the plan breached Section 30(2)(b) of the IBC and Regulation 38(1)(b) of the CIRP Regulations. Dissenting financial creditors were to be paid through NCDs redeemable over six years, not in money.

Plan terms: total outlay Rs. 2,962.02 crores against admitted claims of Rs. 64,838.63 crores (haircut 95.85 per cent). Operational creditors were to get 0.72 per cent. The plan gave financial creditors NCDs of face value Rs. 2,700 crores at a 6.65 per cent coupon and 8 per cent equity in VIL. Liquid

Civil Appeal No. 1307 of 2022, Nos. 8659–8661 of 2026, 8718–8719 of 2026 and Diary No. 41234 of 2026 (promoter Venugopal Dhoot) were dismissed. Diary No. 41286 of 2026 (VIL Vendors Association) was dismissed with liberty to pursue other remedies.

The Court held that assets of foreign and Indian subsidiaries are excluded from VIL's CIRP under the Explanation to Section 18. The Brazil and Nunukan (Indonesia) oil and gas assets are therefore not VIL's assets. The BPRL right-of-first-refusal transaction concluded on 02.07.2026.

The Court held the CoC can revisit its approval and is not functus officio. It refused to confine the CoC to the SRA's existing plan; the CoC can modify that plan or invite fresh plans. The Court also set guardrails on NCLAT remand, including strict timelines.
read: Fact: the Supreme Court has finally rejected the Twinstar plan and the promoter's bid to bring the foreign oil and gas assets into VIL's CIRP. Read: the case goes back to the creditors for a fresh decision. The CoC earlier resolved by 97 per cent to invite fresh expressions of interest (Form G, 18.01.2022), and the Court did not restrict that route. The 2021 plan paid Rs. 2,962.02 crores against Rs. 64,838.63 crores of claims, and the foreign assets are out of the estate. Equity holders were already far behind creditors, and nothing in this order points to any value for them. The order does not mention equity.
positives: Ends a roughly five-year legal stalemate over the plan, so the CoC can now act
The Court stresses timelines on remand, which could speed the next round
Operational creditors and vendors keep the option of fresh bids and other legal remedies
risks: A fresh process could mean another bidding round and a new haircut for all creditors. The order does not say what equity holders get.
Foreign oil and gas assets are confirmed outside VIL's estate, and the BPRL transaction has closed, which removes a possible source of value
Red flag: company has been in CIRP since 2018, and 95.85 per cent haircut and 0.72 per cent operational creditor recovery were on the table in the rejected plan
check_next: Whether the CoC invites fresh expressions of interest or revisits Twinstar's plan, what timeline it sets, and any NCLAT or NCLT directions that follow

headline: CHANDAN: Q2 FY27 standalone PAT ₹18.61 Cr (+224.19% YoY) includes ₹10.23 Cr one-off gain on selling pharmacy arm to group company
facts: Q2 FY27 standalone Total Income ₹59.36 Cr (+44.78% YoY, +19.30% QoQ); EBITDA ₹22.12 Cr (+54.79% YoY); EBITDA margin 37.26% vs 34.85%
Q2 FY27 PAT ₹18.61 Cr vs ₹5.74 Cr (+224.19%); H1 FY27 PAT ₹25.37 Cr vs ₹7.11 Cr; Q1 FY27 PAT was ₹6.76 Cr
PAT, PAT margin and EPS for Q2 and H1 include a one-time exceptional gain of ₹10.23 Cr net of tax (₹12.03 Cr gross) on the sale of the investment in Chandan Pharmacy Limited
Entire 53.56% stake in Chandan Pharmacy Limited sold to Chandan Hospital Limited, a Chandan Group company, for ₹16.77 Cr, based on an independent valuation of CPL at ₹31.31 Cr
Franchise centres were 685 at 30 September 2026 vs 264 at end-June; the release also says 410 were added in the quarter. Target is 1,000 by FY27-end and about 3,000 over the following two years

read: Underlying diagnostics growth looks real: income +44.78% and EBITDA +54.79% YoY in the quarter, with margin up 241 BPS. The headline PAT growth is inflated. Stripping the ₹10.23 Cr net gain (my arithmetic, not the company's), Q2 PAT is about ₹8.38 Cr vs ₹5.74 Cr, and H1 PAT about ₹15.14 Cr vs ₹7.11 Cr. The sale of the pharmacy arm went to a promoter-group company, so it is a related-party deal. The release gives no cash flow, receivables, capex or balance sheet data, so earnings quality cannot be judged from it.
positives: EBITDA margin 37.26% in Q2, with EBITDA growth (+54.79%) ahead of income growth (+44.78%)

headline: PARAMOUNT DYE TEC: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 3864.19 lakh vs Rs 3090.06 lakh a year ago, but PAT fell to Rs 138.05 lakh from Rs 216.47 lakh
facts: Half year ended 30 Sep 2026 (unaudited): revenue from operations Rs 3864.19 lakh vs Rs 3090.06 lakh in H1 FY26 and Rs 4289.48 lakh in H2 FY26.

Profit before tax Rs 170.31 lakh vs Rs 244.55 lakh a year ago. Profit after tax Rs 138.05 lakh vs Rs 216.47 lakh. Basic and diluted EPS Rs 1.99 (H1 FY26: Rs 4.81; H2 FY26: Rs -0.05). Other income Rs 74.64 lakh vs Rs 83.24 lakh.

The auditor's limited review report carries an Emphasis of Matter. There was no physical verification of inventories at 30 Sep 2026, and no direct balance confirmations or external verification of trade receivables and payables. The auditor relied on a certificate from an independent CA and on manag

Balance sheet at 30 Sep 2026 vs 31 Mar 2026: trade receivables Rs 2668.19 lakh vs Rs 1843.15 lakh. Inventory Rs 3570.68 lakh vs Rs 3536.47 lakh. Non-current borrowings Rs 1197.09 lakh vs Rs 217.99 lakh. Current borrowings Rs 360.86 lakh vs Rs 1427.28 lakh. Total equity Rs 6710.75 lakh.
Cash flow statement: net cash from operating activities Rs 804.47 lakh for the half, vs Rs -2175.41 lakh for FY26. Investing Rs -643.45 lakh. Financing Rs -162.65 lakh. Closing cash Rs 51.31 lakh.

FY26 had an exceptional item of Rs 448.27 lakh in H2, with no nature stated in the results table. Full-year FY26 PAT was Rs 214.23 lakh vs Rs 800.29 lakh in FY25. The board met on 14 Nov 2026 and the outcome was filed on 17 Nov 2026.
read: Fact: sales grew about 25% year on year (my calculation), but profit fell about 36% and PBT margin fell to about 4.4% from about 7.9%. Read: this is growth without earnings growth, with thin margins and a working-capital-heavy business. Receivables plus inventory (Rs 6238.87 lakh) are about 63% of total assets. The positive operating cash flow comes from working-capital items, not from profit, and the cash flow statement is poorly laid out. The auditor's emphasis on unverified inventory and receivables lowers confidence in the balance sheet, which is where most of the risk sits.

headline: SML MAHINDRA: Rights issue up to ₹1,449.65 cr at ₹3,506.00/share, 2 for 7; funds ₹525.00 cr buy of M&M truck and bus unit
facts: Issue of up to 4,134,756 equity shares at ₹3,506.00 each (premium ₹3,496.00), aggregating up to ₹1,449.65 crores; ratio 2 shares for every 7 held; record date November 20, 2026
Issue opens December 1, 2026, closes December 9, 2026, listing December 14, 2026. The issue is not underwritten. Net proceeds ₹1,444.23 crores
Use of net proceeds: ₹525.00 crores to buy M&M's truck and bus division (MTBD); ₹125.00 crores capex; ₹450.00 crores R&D; ₹344.23 crores general corporate purposes
MTBD carve-out, certified by M&M's CFO: FY26 revenue ₹2,982.71 crores, EBITDA ₹60.68 crores, EBIT ₹(8.03) crores. FY25 EBITDA was ₹4.79 crores and FY24 EBITDA was ₹(68.38) crores

Promoter M&M holds 58.97%. It intends to take up its full entitlement and any unsubscribed portion up to the issue size, subject to takeover rules. Ex-rights price stated as ₹5235.33
read: This is a large recapitalisation tied to a related-party deal. The issue is about 2.6 times September 2026 net worth (₹1,449.65 crores against ₹559.91 crores), and it adds 4,134,756 shares to 14,471,646 paid-up (my arithmetic, about 28.6%). It buys a division with higher revenue than SML (₹2,982.71 crores against ₹2,837.92 crores in FY26) that is barely profitable at EBITDA and loss-making at EBIT. Only ₹525.00 crores of the ₹1,444.23 crores net proceeds goes to the acquisition. About ₹794 crores (₹450.00 crores R&D plus ₹344.23 crores general purposes) is loosely defined, and none of it has been appraised by a bank or other outside agency. The money goes largely to the promoter, which is also the dominant subscriber and the backstop.

headline: INDIA GLYCOLS: First post-demerger results, Q2 FY27 revenue Rs. 358.18 Crore, EBITDA Rs. 39.34 Crore, PAT Rs. 11.24 Crore
facts: Q2 FY27 (unaudited, standalone): revenue from operations Rs. 358.18 Crore, EBITDA Rs. 39.34 Crore, PAT Rs. 11.24 Crore, quarterly EPS Rs. 1.68
Q1 FY27, restated for the demerger: revenue Rs. 354.64 Crore, EBITDA Rs. 40.21 Crore, PAT Rs. 12.35 Crore, EPS Rs. 1.84
H1 FY27: revenue Rs. 712.82 Crore, EBITDA Rs. 79.55 Crore, PAT Rs. 23.59 Crore, EPS Rs. 3.52

The Spirits & Biofuel Undertaking went to IGL Spirits Limited and the Biopharma Undertaking went to Ennature Bio Pharma Limited. The scheme became effective September 1, 2026, with an appointed date of April 1, 2026
The company says the Q2 FY26 comparative (revenue Rs. 2,410.71 Crore, PAT Rs. 53.94 Crore) includes the demerged units and is not comparable
The continuing business is Biobased Specialty Materials, Sustainable & Performance Chemicals, and Gases
read: The year-on-year drop in the headline numbers comes from the demerger and means nothing about operations. The only usable comparison is Q2 against the restated Q1. On the figures given, revenue is up about 1.0% (358.18 vs 354.64), EBITDA is down about 2.2% and PAT is down about 9.0%. That is flat to slightly softer. India Glycols is now a much smaller chemicals-and-gases company. Q2 revenue of Rs. 358.18 Crore is about 15% of the Rs. 2,410.71 Crore reported a year ago, which included the demerged units. The release gives no segment split, no margin commentary and no guidance.
positives: The demerger is completed and the continuing business is now a pure bio-based chemicals and gases company
Q2 revenue is steady against restated Q1 (Rs. 358.18 Crore vs Rs. 354.64 Crore)
H1 EPS of Rs. 3.52 equals Q1 plus Q2 (1.84 + 1.68), so the numbers are internally consistent
risks: Profit fell for the second quarter in a row on restated numbers, with PAT at Rs. 11.24 Crore vs Rs. 12.35 Crore. EBITDA also slipped
The release has no segment data, no balance sheet, no cash flow and no debt allocation after the demerger, so quality and leverage cannot be judged
The press release has no valid history, and the results are unaudited. The restated base is only one prior quarter

headline: BHARAT FORGE: Wholly owned subsidiary Ferrovia Transrail merged into BF Infrastructure, effective Nov 17, 2026; both had NIL FY26 revenue
facts: Regional Director, Western Region order dated November 5, 2026 approved the merger of Ferrovia Transrail Solutions Pvt Ltd (transferor) into BF Infrastructure Ltd (transferee) under Section 233 of the Companies Act, 2013
The Scheme became effective on November 17, 2026, when the order was filed with the Registrar of Companies, Maharashtra. The transferor company stands dissolved
Turnover/revenue from operations for year ended March 31, 2026: BFIL NIL; FTSPL NIL
Both entities are wholly owned subsidiaries, so there is no cash consideration and no new shares are issued
Both entities are in engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) and infrastructure development projects
Bharat Forge is not a party to the Scheme and its shareholding pattern remains unchanged
read: This is an internal tidy-up inside the group. Both entities reported NIL revenue for FY26, so the merger moves no earnings, assets or cash that the filing quantifies. The stated reason is synergy and lower operating cost, but with no revenue in either entity the saving looks small. It does not change the investment case for Bharat Forge.
positives: No dilution, no cash outflow, no change in Bharat Forge's shareholding
Fewer group entities to run and report on
risks: Rationale is generic; no size, cost saving or project pipeline is given
Both entities had NIL revenue, so the EPC/infrastructure arm shows no operating track record in this filing

headline: ACME SOLAR: ACME Greentech Sixteen signs PPA with RUMSL for 220 MW Solar+BESS at Morena, MP, at Rs. 2.764 per unit
facts: Counterparty is Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Limited (RUMSL), a domestic, unlisted entity. The filing says it has no promoter or related-party link.
ACME Greentech Sixteen Private Limited executed a Power Purchase Agreement for a 220 MW (Unit II) Solar with Battery Energy Storage System project at Morena Solar Park, Madhya Pradesh.
Tariff is Rs. 2.764 per unit. Project tenure is 25 years from the date of signing of the PPA.
Scheduled commercial operation date (SCOD) is December 31, 2027.
Amount of the order is stated as 16950000000 INR.
The filing gives the date of bagging/receiving as 2026-02-09. The event occurrence date is 2026-11-16 at 15:26, and the report date is 2026-11-17.
read: This is a new 220 MW solar+storage asset with a 25-year PPA. It adds to ACME's contracted pipeline, but it is a build-and-own project, not a service order, so it will not produce revenue until construction is done. The filing does not say what the 16950000000 INR figure represents (project cost or lifetime revenue), and it gives no company revenue or net worth to compare against, so I cannot size it against the company. The 2026-02-09 date against the 2026-11-16 event date does not line up and may mean a late disclosure or a data error.

headline: SUPREME PETROCHEM: Versalis licence signed for 2nd 70 KTPA mABS line, Rs 450 crores, internal accruals, mechanical completion Dec 2028
facts: Technology Agreement with Versalis S.p.A, Italy for 2nd line of 70 KTPA of mABS was entered into on November 12, 2026. The signed copy arrived on November 17, 2026.
